## Get Volatility and Deltas

```{r}
get_vol_df <- function(nport,crsp){
  
  nport <- bind_rows(nport)
  
  #create key to join on
  
  key_df <- nport %>%
    distinct(adj_period_of_report) %>%
    mutate(
      quarter_indicator = case_when(
        month(adj_period_of_report) %in% c(1, 4, 7, 10) ~ 1,
        month(adj_period_of_report) %in% c(2, 5, 8, 11) ~ 2,
        month(adj_period_of_report) %in% c(3, 6, 9, 12) ~ 3,
        TRUE ~ NA_real_ # For any other cases
        )) %>%
    group_by(quarter_indicator) %>%
    mutate(window_start = dplyr::lag(adj_period_of_report),
           key = paste0(
             month(window_start),
             "to",
             month(adj_period_of_report),
             "_",
             year(adj_period_of_report)
             )) %>%
    select(adj_period_of_report, window_start, quarter_indicator, key) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    drop_na()
  
  crsp_key <- crsp %>% 
    left_join(key_df, 
              join_by(date > window_start,
                      date <= adj_period_of_report))

  nport_key <- nport %>% left_join(key_df, by = "adj_period_of_report")
  
  #calculate log returns from crsp
  returns_df <- crsp_key %>%
    group_by(ISIN, quarter_indicator) %>%
    arrange(date) %>%
    mutate(
      log_ret = log(adj_prc) - log(dplyr::lag(adj_prc))
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(log_ret)) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  quarterly_vol <- returns_df %>%
    group_by(ISIN, key) %>%
    summarise(
     vol = sd(log_ret),
      .groups = "drop"
   )
  
  
  nport_vol <- nport_key %>%
  left_join(
    quarterly_vol %>% select(ISIN, key, vol),
    by = c("isin" = "ISIN", "key")
  ) %>%
  select(series_id, isin, adj_period_of_report, 
         adj_balance, adj_prc, notional_prc, 
         notional_prc_delta, bal_delta, key, vol)

  ##### Modify this because we are not working with notional price since they cancel out
  final_df <- nport_vol %>%
    group_by(isin, adj_period_of_report) %>%
    mutate(
      quarter_fund_value = sum(notional_prc, na.rm = TRUE), #this remains the same so we have notional fund value
      balance_sum = sum(adj_balance, na.rm = TRUE), #for an internal check
      normalized_holdings = adj_balance/sum(adj_balance, na.rm = TRUE) #this was changed but not name - adjusted notional price does not actually exist
      ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    arrange(isin, series_id, adj_period_of_report)
    
  final_df <- final_df %>%
    arrange(isin, series_id, adj_period_of_report) %>%
    group_by(series_id, isin) %>%
    mutate(normalized_holding_delta = c(NA, diff(normalized_holdings))) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    drop_na(normalized_holding_delta)
  
  return(list(quarterly_vol, nport_vol, final_df))
}
```

## Rolling Window Pipeline

```{r}
#Step 1: Gets trading dates that we will loop over
get_signal_months <- function(prepped_data, window_months = 24) {
  
  all_months    <- sort(unique(prepped_data$adj_period_of_report))
  signal_months <- all_months[all_months >= min(all_months) + months(window_months)]
  
  cat(sprintf("Total months in data:  %d\n", length(all_months)))
  cat(sprintf("Signal months:         %d\n", length(signal_months)))
  cat(sprintf("First signal month:    %s\n", min(signal_months)))
  cat(sprintf("Last signal month:     %s\n", max(signal_months)))
  
  signal_months
}

#Step 2: Split data using rolling window and
slice_training_window <- function(prepped_data, window_end, window_months = 24) {
  
  # Ensure window_end is in Date format
  window_end <- as.Date(window_end)
  
  # Extract unique report dates from data
  all_months <- sort(unique(prepped_data$adj_period_of_report))
  
  # Find the position of the user's window_end
  end_idx <- which(all_months == window_end)
  
  if (length(end_idx) == 0) {
    stop(sprintf("The provided window_end (%s) was not found in adj_period_of_report.", window_end))
  }
  
  # Calculate start index based on unique data periods (inclusive of end date)
  start_idx    <- max(1, end_idx - window_months)
  window_start <- all_months[start_idx]
  
  # Filter the data using the calculated start and end dates
  result <- prepped_data %>%
    filter(adj_period_of_report >= window_start,
           adj_period_of_report <= window_end)
  
  return(result)
}

#Step 3: Set a min number of assets held by a split into buyer and seller dataframes
split_buyers_sellers <- function(train_data, min_assets = 10) {
  
  total_assets <- train_data %>%
    group_by(series_id) %>%
    filter(adj_period_of_report == min(adj_period_of_report)) %>%
    filter(n() >= min_assets)
  
  buyers <- train_data %>%
    filter(delta_sign == 1) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  sellers <- train_data %>%
    filter(delta_sign == -1) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  cat(sprintf("Buyers:  %d rows | %d funds (dropped %d funds below min_assets)\n",
              nrow(buyers),
              n_distinct(buyers$series_id),
              n_distinct(train_data$series_id) - n_distinct(buyers$series_id)))
  cat(sprintf("Sellers: %d rows | %d funds (dropped %d funds below min_assets)\n",
              nrow(sellers),
              n_distinct(sellers$series_id),
              n_distinct(train_data$series_id) - n_distinct(sellers$series_id)))
  
  list(buyers = buyers, sellers = sellers)
}

#Step 4: Obtain the dominant sector of each fund for the training dataframe window
get_dominant_sectors <- function(train_df, percent = 0.25) {
  
  # 1. Sort Sectors and calculate proportions based on the earliest report period
  sector_sorting <- train_df %>%
    group_by(series_id) %>%
    filter(adj_period_of_report == min(adj_period_of_report, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    group_by(series_id, adj_period_of_report, SECTORS) %>%
    summarise(sector_total = sum(notional_prc, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop_last") %>%
    mutate(proportion = sector_total / sum(sector_total)) %>%
    ungroup()

  # 2. Isolate the row with the highest proportion for each fund
  dominant_sector_df <- sector_sorting %>% 
    group_by(series_id) %>%
    slice_max(proportion, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(
      dominant_sector = if_else(
        proportion >= percent, 
        as.character(SECTORS), 
        "No Dominant Sector"
      )
    ) %>%
    select(series_id, dominant_sector, max_proportion = proportion) %>%
    group_by(dominant_sector) %>%
    arrange(desc(max_proportion), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    ungroup() # Un-grouping at the end keeps the output dataframe clean
    
  return(dominant_sector_df)
}
```

## LME Models

```{r}
fit_lme_models <- function(split_data) {
  
  fit_one <- function(df, label) {
    tryCatch(
      {
        m <- lmer(boxcox_delta ~ 1 + vol + (1 + vol | series_id) + (1 | isin),
                  data = df)
        cat(sprintf("%s model: converged = %s | fixed vol = %.4f\n",
                    label,
                    !any(grepl("failed to converge", m@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages %||% "")),
                    fixef(m)["vol"]))
        m
      },
      error = function(e) {
        cat(sprintf("%s model FAILED: %s\n", label, e$message))
        NULL
      }
    )
  }
  
  list(
    buyer_model  = fit_one(split_data$buyers,  "Buyer"),
    seller_model = fit_one(split_data$sellers, "Seller")
  )
}

extract_random_effects <- function(model, grpvar_filter, term_filter, ci_level = 0.95, sector_df = NULL) {
  
  # 1. Calculate CI multiplier
  z <- qnorm(1 - (1 - ci_level) / 2)
  
  # 2. Extract and filter random effects
  re_df <- as.data.frame(lme4::ranef(model, condVar = TRUE)) %>%
    filter(grpvar == grpvar_filter & term == term_filter)
  
  if (nrow(re_df) == 0) {
    stop("No data found matching the provided grpvar_filter and term_filter.")
  }
  
  # 3. Calculate CIs and build primary dataframe
  result_df <- re_df %>%
    mutate(
      lower  = condval - z * condsd,
      upper  = condval + z * condsd,
      signal = ifelse(lower > 0, "Positive Signal",
               ifelse(upper < 0, "Negative Signal", "No Signal"))
    ) %>%
    select(
      group        = grp, 
      term,
      beta         = condval,
      se           = condsd,
      lower_ci     = lower,
      upper_ci     = upper,
      signal
    ) %>%
    mutate(group = as.character(group))
  
  # 4. Join sector data
  if (!is.null(sector_df)) {
    result_df <- result_df %>%
      left_join(sector_df, by = c("group" = "series_id"))
  } else {
    result_df$dominant_sector <- "Unknown"
  }
  
  # Add metadata attributes for the plotting functions to use in titles/subtitles
  attr(result_df, "grpvar_filter") <- grpvar_filter
  attr(result_df, "term_filter")   <- term_filter
  attr(result_df, "ci_level")      <- ci_level
  
  return(result_df)
}
```

```{r}
generate_summary_row <- function(beta_df, current_date) {
  
  row_df <- beta_df %>%
    # 1. Calculate total number of funds per sector
    group_by(dominant_sector) %>%
    mutate(sector_total = n()) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    
    # 2. Count occurrences of each signal per sector
    count(dominant_sector, signal, sector_total) %>%
    
    # 3. Calculate the proportion
    mutate(proportion = n / sector_total) %>%
    
    # 4. Clean strings for column names
    mutate(
      dominant_sector = tolower(str_replace_all(dominant_sector, " ", "_")),
      signal = case_when(
        signal == "Positive Signal" ~ "positive",
        signal == "Negative Signal" ~ "negative",
        TRUE ~ "no_signal"
      )
    ) %>%
    
    # =========================================================================
    # THE FIX: Force both 'positive' and 'negative' rows to exist for every sector.
    # If they are missing, fill their 'proportion' with 0.
    # =========================================================================
    complete(
      dominant_sector, 
      signal = c("positive", "negative"), 
      fill = list(proportion = 0)
    ) %>%
    
    # 5. Filter for significant signals (no_signal rows drop out here)
    filter(signal %in% c("positive", "negative")) %>%
    
    # 6. Drop metadata columns to ensure a single-row pivot
    select(dominant_sector, signal, proportion) %>% 
    
    # 7. Pivot to wide format
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = c(dominant_sector, signal),
      names_sep = "-",
      values_from = proportion
    ) %>%
    
    # 8. Append the end_date to the front
    mutate(end_date = current_date, .before = 1)
  
  return(row_df)
}
```

```{r}
# 1. Initialize storage lists for models and raw betas
all_models          <- list()
all_betas           <- list()

# 2. Initialize storage lists for the summary rows
buyer_summary_rows  <- list()
seller_summary_rows <- list()

signal_months <- get_signal_months(delta_df, window_months = 24)

for (i in 1:length(signal_months)) {
  window_max      <- signal_months[i] 
  current_month   <- as.character(window_max) 
  
  # Data prep pipeline
  train           <- slice_training_window(delta_df, window_max, window_months = 24)
  dominant_sector <- get_dominant_sectors(train)
  split           <- split_buyers_sellers(train, min_assets = 10)
  
  # Fit the models
  models          <- fit_lme_models(split)
  all_models[[current_month]] <- models
  
  # Extract random effects (checking for NULLs if a model failed)
  buyer_beta  <- NULL
  seller_beta <- NULL
  
  if (!is.null(models$buyer_model)) {
    buyer_beta <- extract_random_effects(
      model         = models$buyer_model, 
      grpvar_filter = "series_id", 
      term_filter   = "vol", 
      sector_df     = dominant_sector
    )
    
    # Generate and store the summary row for Buyers
    buyer_summary_rows[[current_month]] <- generate_summary_row(buyer_beta, window_max)
  }
  
  if (!is.null(models$seller_model)) {
    seller_beta <- extract_random_effects(
      model         = models$seller_model, 
      grpvar_filter = "series_id", 
      term_filter   = "vol", 
      sector_df     = dominant_sector
    )
    
    # Generate and store the summary row for Sellers
    seller_summary_rows[[current_month]] <- generate_summary_row(seller_beta, window_max)
  }
  
  # Store raw betas
  all_betas[[current_month]] <- list(
    buyer_beta  = buyer_beta,
    seller_beta = seller_beta
  )
  print(paste("Done with iteration", i))
}

# =========================================================================
# AFTER THE LOOP: Combine the individual rows into master dataframes
# =========================================================================
buyer_summary_table  <- bind_rows(buyer_summary_rows)
seller_summary_table <- bind_rows(seller_summary_rows)
```

```{r}
plot_re_combined <- function(model,
                             grpvar_filter,
                             term_filter,
                             ci_level = 0.95,
                             sector_df = NULL,
                             order_list = NULL, 
                             title = "Random Effects & Signal Analysis", 
                             subtitle = NULL,
                             rel_widths = c(2, 1)) {
  
  # 1. Extract random effects data from the fitted lme4 model
  beta_df <- extract_random_effects(
    model         = model,
    grpvar_filter = grpvar_filter,
    term_filter   = term_filter,
    ci_level      = ci_level,
    sector_df     = sector_df
  )
  
  # 2. Check Metadata & Warnings
  if (all(beta_df$dominant_sector == "Unknown")) {
    warning("sector_df was not provided during extraction; all sectors are labeled 'Unknown'.")
  }
  
  # Standardize Signal factor levels and colors across both plots
  signal_levels <- c("Positive Signal", "Negative Signal", "No Signal")
  signal_colors <- c(
    "Positive Signal" = "#4E79A7",
    "Negative Signal" = "#F28E2B",
    "No Signal"       = "#BAB0AC"
  )
  
  beta_df <- beta_df %>%
    mutate(signal = factor(signal, levels = signal_levels))
  
  # Apply Group Ordering (if specified)
  if (!is.null(order_list)) {
    beta_df <- beta_df %>%
      mutate(group = factor(group, levels = order_list)) %>%
      arrange(group)
  }
  
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Plot 1: Caterpillar Plot (Faceted Wide)
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  p1_data <- beta_df %>%
    arrange(desc(signal == "No Signal"))
  
  p1 <- ggplot(p1_data, aes(x = group, y = beta, color = signal)) +
    geom_point(size = 2.5) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower_ci, ymax = upper_ci), width = 0.3) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
    scale_color_manual(values = signal_colors, drop = FALSE) +
    facet_grid(
      . ~ dominant_sector, 
      scales = "free_x", 
      switch = "x", 
      labeller = label_wrap_gen(width = 12)
    ) +
    labs(
      x = "Dominant Sector",
      y = "Random Effect"
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x      = element_blank(),  
      axis.ticks.x     = element_blank(),
      strip.background = element_blank(),     
      strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 7, angle = 45, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5), 
      panel.spacing    = unit(0.8, "lines")
    ) +
    guides(color = "none")  # Prevents duplicate/redundant legend
  
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Plot 2: Normal Barplot (Signal Counts)
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  p2_data <- beta_df %>%
    count(dominant_sector, signal, .drop = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(signal = factor(signal, levels = c("No Signal", "Negative Signal", "Positive Signal")))
  
  p2 <- ggplot(p2_data, aes(x = dominant_sector, y = n, fill = signal)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE), width = 0.7) +
    scale_fill_manual(name = "Signal Type", values = signal_colors, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = scales::label_wrap(12)) + # Match 12-char label wrapping of p1
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) + # Flush baseline at y = 0
    labs(
      x = "Dominant Sector",
      y = "Number of Funds"
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        face   = "bold",
        size   = 7,       # Matches p1 font size
        angle  = 45,
        hjust  = 1,       # Anchors label text flush against ticks
        vjust  = 1
      )
    )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Combine Plots with Shared Title
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  combined_plot <- (p1 + wrap_elements(p2)) +
    plot_layout(widths = rel_widths) +
    plot_annotation(
      title    = title,
      subtitle = subtitle,
      theme    = theme(
        plot.title    = element_text(hjust = 0, face = "bold", size = 14),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 11)
      )
    )

  print(combined_plot)
  
  return(list(
    data          = invisible(beta_df), 
    bar_data      = invisible(p2_data), 
    combined_plot = combined_plot
  ))
}
```

```{r}
#pull a specific sector facet from Caterpillar Plot
plot_re_sector <- function(model,
                           grpvar_filter,
                           term_filter,
                           target_sector,
                           ci_level = 0.95,
                           sector_df = NULL,
                           order_list = NULL, 
                           title = NULL, 
                           subtitle = NULL) {
  
  # 1. Extract random effects data from the fitted lme4 model
  beta_df <- extract_random_effects(
    model         = model,
    grpvar_filter = grpvar_filter,
    term_filter   = term_filter,
    ci_level      = ci_level,
    sector_df     = sector_df
  )
  
  # 2. Check sector metadata & filter for the target sector
  if (all(beta_df$dominant_sector == "Unknown")) {
    warning("sector_df was not provided during extraction; all sectors are labeled 'Unknown'.")
  }
  
  beta_df_filtered <- beta_df %>%
    filter(dominant_sector == target_sector)
  
  if (nrow(beta_df_filtered) == 0) {
    stop(sprintf("Target sector '%s' was not found in the dataset.", target_sector))
  }
  
  # Set default dynamic title if none is provided
  if (is.null(title)) {
    title <- paste("Random Effects Analysis:", target_sector)
  }
  
  # Standardize Signal factor levels and colors
  signal_levels <- c("Positive Signal", "Negative Signal", "No Signal")
  signal_colors <- c(
    "Positive Signal" = "#4E79A7",
    "Negative Signal" = "#F28E2B",
    "No Signal"       = "#BAB0AC"
  )
  
  beta_df_filtered <- beta_df_filtered %>%
    mutate(signal = factor(signal, levels = signal_levels))
  
  # Apply Group Ordering (if specified)
  if (!is.null(order_list)) {
    beta_df_filtered <- beta_df_filtered %>%
      mutate(group = factor(group, levels = order_list)) %>%
      arrange(group)
  }
  
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Faceted Caterpillar Plot (Single Sector)
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  p_data <- beta_df_filtered %>%
    arrange(desc(signal == "No Signal"))
  
  p <- ggplot(p_data, aes(x = group, y = beta, color = signal)) +
    geom_point(size = 2.5) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower_ci, ymax = upper_ci), width = 0.3) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
    scale_color_manual(name = "Signal Type", values = signal_colors, drop = FALSE) +
    facet_grid(
      . ~ dominant_sector, 
      scales = "free_x", 
      switch = "x", 
      labeller = label_wrap_gen(width = 20)
    ) +
    labs(
      title    = title,
      subtitle = subtitle,
      x        = "Dominant Sector",
      y        = "Random Effect"
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      plot.title       = element_text(hjust = 0, face = "bold", size = 14),
      plot.subtitle    = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 11),
      axis.text.x      = element_blank(),  
      axis.ticks.x     = element_blank(),
      strip.background = element_blank(),     
      strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9, angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5), 
      panel.spacing    = unit(0.8, "lines")
    )

  print(p)
  
  return(list(
    data = invisible(beta_df_filtered), 
    plot = p
  ))
}
```

Sensitivity Analysis - Buy Side

```{r}
dec_buy_data <- dec24_buy@frame

set.seed(42)

# 1. Assign folds randomly within each fund to ensure balanced group coverage
dec_buy_data <- dec_buy_data %>%
  group_by(series_id) %>%
  mutate(fold = sample(rep(1:5, length.out = n()))) %>%
  ungroup()

cv_preds_buy <- numeric(nrow(dec_buy_data))

# 2. Run 5-fold CV
for (k in 1:5) {
  train <- filter(dec_buy_data, fold != k)
  test  <- filter(dec_buy_data, fold == k)
  
  # Fit LMM on training set
  fit_cv <- lmer(boxcox_delta ~ 1 + vol + (1 + vol | series_id) + (1 | isin), data = train)
  
  # Predict on test set using existing fund/asset random effects
  # allow.new.levels = TRUE handles any unseen fund/asset combinations safely
  cv_preds_buy[dec_buy_data$fold == k] <- predict(fit_cv, newdata = test, allow.new.levels = TRUE)
}

# 3. Calculate Out-of-Sample Conditional R-squared
ss_res <- sum((dec_buy_data$boxcox_delta - cv_preds_buy)^2)
ss_tot <- sum((dec_buy_data$boxcox_delta - mean(dec_buy_data$boxcox_delta))^2)
r2_cond_cv_buy <- 1 - (ss_res / ss_tot)

cat("LOO CV Conditional R-Squared:", r2_cond_cv_buy)
```

```{r}
#filtering out holding delta outliers (>0.05 in raw delta)
filter.05 <- split$buyers %>%
  filter(abs(normalized_holding_delta) <= .05)

dec.05_model <- lmer(boxcox_delta ~ 1 + vol + (1 + vol | series_id) + (1 | isin), data = filter.05)
summary(dec.05_model)
r.squaredGLMM(dec.05_model)
```

```{r}
#filtering out funds that have less than 5 data points
dec_data_summary_buy <- dec_buy_data %>%
  group_by(series_id) %>%
  summarise(observations_per_fund = n())

filter_funds <- dec_data_summary_buy %>%
  filter(observations_per_fund > 5) %>%
  select(c("series_id"))

larger_funds <- dec_buy_data %>% filter(series_id %in% filter_funds$series_id)

dec_large_model <- lmer(boxcox_delta ~ 1 + vol + (1 + vol | series_id) + (1 | isin), 
                        data = larger_funds)
summary(dec_large_model)
r.squaredGLMM(dec_large_model)
```
